\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Complement of SAT in polynomial oracle time]
\lean{Complexity.compl_SAT_mem_POracle_SAT}
\label{Complexity.compl_SAT_mem_POracle_SAT}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.POracle, Complexity.SAT, Complexity.compl_mem_POracle, Complexity.oracle_mem_POracle}
\difficulty{1}
Let $	extsf{SAT}$ be the language of bit strings whose decoded CNF formulas are
satisfiable, with malformed strings decoded as the empty formula. The complement of
$	extsf{SAT}$ is decidable in polynomial time by a finite oracle Turing machine with
oracle $	extsf{SAT}$; equivalently, $	extsf{SAT}^{c} \in \mathsf{P}^{\textsf{SAT}}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[NP languages and a SAT oracle]
\lean{Complexity.NP_subset_POracle_SAT}
\label{Complexity.NP_subset_POracle_SAT}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.POracle, Complexity.SAT, Complexity.SAT_NPHard, Complexity.mem_POracle_of_polyTimeReducible}
\difficulty{1}
Every language in $\mathrm{NP}$ belongs to $\mathrm{P}^{\mathrm{SAT}}$: it is decidable
in polynomial time by a deterministic Turing machine with an oracle for the language of
bit strings whose decoded CNF formulas are satisfiable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[CoNP and SAT-oracle polynomial time]
\lean{Complexity.coNP_subset_POracle_SAT}
\label{Complexity.coNP_subset_POracle_SAT}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP_subset_POracle_SAT, Complexity.POracle, Complexity.SAT, Complexity.coNP, Complexity.compl_mem_POracle}
\difficulty{3}
Let a language be a set of finite binary strings. Define $	ext{NP}$ to consist of
languages $L$ for which there are fixed nonnegative integers $C,c$ and a language $V$
decidable in deterministic polynomial time such that, for every string $x$, membership
$x\in L$ is equivalent to the existence of a string $u$ of length exactly $C(|x|+1)^c$
with $xu\in V$. Let $	ext{coNP}$ consist of languages whose complements belong to
$	ext{NP}$. Let $	ext{SAT}$ be the language of binary strings whose decoded conjunctive
normal form is satisfiable, with strings that fail to parse decoded as the empty
formula. Let $	ext{P}^{\text{SAT}}$ consist of languages decidable by a deterministic
oracle Turing machine with access to $	ext{SAT}$ in time at most $a(n^d+1)$ for some
fixed nonnegative integers $a,d$. Then $\text{coNP}\subseteq\text{P}^{\text{SAT}}$.
\end{theorem}
